theme: Why a very small first request is often the easiest way to get a larger one accepted, told through a new hire's first month at a newspaper office.

grammar.structure: 原因 + 难怪/怪不得 + 结果（先知道原因，再说“原来如此”）
grammar.explain_en: Use 难怪 or 怪不得 when you have just learned a reason and it suddenly explains something you had already noticed. The cause comes first — either earlier in the same sentence or in the previous sentence — and what follows the adverb is the fact that is now explained: 难怪你今天这么精神，原来昨晚早睡了。 Both words go immediately before the subject of the clause, never at the end of it, and both can stand alone as a one-word reaction: 难怪！/ 怪不得！ 难怪 is neutral and slightly more written. 怪不得 is the everyday spoken form and often takes 了 or 啊 after it: 怪不得他这么高兴。 难怪 can also be followed by 原来 to spell the cause out. Neither word asks a question and neither means 'strange' — for that, use 奇怪. Compare 难怪 with 原来: 原来 simply reports the newly found fact, while 难怪 adds the speaker's reaction, 'that explains it'. If the clause after the adverb is only a guess rather than something you now understand, use 大概 or 也许 instead.
grammar.common_mistake: Learners often put 难怪 in front of the cause, as in 难怪下雨，他没带伞, when the cause must come first: 他没带伞，难怪淋湿了。 A second slip is using 难怪 to translate 'strange'; 奇怪 is the word for that.

examples.zh: 难怪你今天这么精神，原来昨晚早睡了。
examples.py: nán guài nǐ jīn tiān zhè me jīng shén yuán lái zuó wǎn zǎo shuì le
examples.en: No wonder you are so energetic today — you went to bed early last night.

examples.zh: 怪不得大家都赞成这个方案，它确实省时间。
examples.py: guài bu de dà jiā dōu zàn chéng zhè ge fāng àn tā què shí shěng shí jiān
examples.en: No wonder everyone approves of this plan; it really does save time.

examples.zh: 他报告写得那么清楚，难怪经理总让他处理急事。
examples.py: tā bào gào xiě de nà me qīng chu nán guài jīng lǐ zǒng ràng tā chǔ lǐ jí shì
examples.en: His reports are so clear that it is no wonder the manager always asks him to handle urgent matters.

drills.q: 他连着值了三天班，____今天开会时一直打哈欠。
drills.explain: 难怪 introduces the explanation after a known cause: he worked three night shifts, so the yawning is no surprise. 难道 only appears in rhetorical questions, 反而 marks a contrast with expectation, and 简直 exaggerates a description; none of them means 'no wonder'.

drills.q: ____他这么熟悉这条街，原来他在这里住了十年。
drills.explain: 怪不得 fits the pattern reaction-first, reason-after: the 原来 clause supplies the cause. 不得不 means 'have to', 了不起 is an adjective meaning 'amazing', and 由不得 means 'not up to someone' — all are wrong parts of speech here.

reading.title: 第一件小事
reading.text:
刚进报社那年，我被安排给一位老编辑当助手。第一天轮到我值班，他只让我把一段三百字的消息看一遍，回来告诉他有没有错字。事情太小，我没有犹豫就答应了。
第三天，他让我帮忙处理一封读者来信；一个星期以后，我已经在替他整理短评了。月底总结会上，我看见自己的名字第一次出现在报纸上。同事笑着说，这位编辑最会用这种办法带新人。先给一个很低的门槛，你点了头，后面的事就不觉得难。
我这才明白，怪不得他从来不催人，也从不勉强谁。那种被信任的感觉，比任何报告都更让人迫切地想把下一步做好。
reading.translation:
The year I joined the newspaper office, I was assigned as an assistant to a senior editor. On my first day on duty, he asked me only to read a three-hundred-character news item and tell him whether there were any typos. The task was so small that I agreed without hesitating.
On the third day he asked me to help handle a reader's letter; a week later I was already sorting his short commentaries. At the month-end review meeting I saw my own name in the paper for the first time. A colleague laughed and said this editor was a master at bringing new people along: give them a very low threshold first, and once they nod, the rest no longer feels difficult.
Only then did I understand — no wonder he never rushed anyone and never forced anyone. That feeling of being trusted made me more eager to do the next step well than any written report could.

options: 一位编辑怎样一步步带新人
新人怎样写出一篇短评
总结会上如何汇报工作
questions.explain: The passage follows the assistant's tasks from reading a short news item to sorting short commentaries, all arranged by the senior editor, so the focus is his step-by-step way of training a newcomer.

questions.q: 作者第一天值班时，被安排做的是____。
questions.explain: The first paragraph says that on his first day on duty he was asked to read a three-hundred-character news item and report whether there were any typos.

questions.q: 从文章最后一段看，作者对老编辑的做法____。
questions.explain: The closing sentence says the trust made him eager to do the next step well, and he uses 怪不得 to show he now understands the method — clear approval rather than doubt.

dictation: 他值班的时候从来不接私人电话。
社区请我帮忙处理一份报告。
我没有犹豫就答应了这件事。
他劝我先实践一个月再作决定。
那位编辑说话很谦虚，也不轻易批评人。

writing.prompt: Describe a small first step at work that later led to something bigger. What did you hesitate about, what did you agree to, and what changed afterwards? Use the words below.
writing.model: 上个月主管让我试着处理客户来信。我有些犹豫，怕自己写不好。第一封只有两百字，我改了三遍才发出去；两周后我独立写了一份报告，才发现最难的是开头那一步。这件事让我更愿意在实践中学习，也让我明白：把小事做好，后面的路自然会宽一点。
writing.tips: Start with the request and your hesitation, add one concrete detail about the first small task, then close with what that first step changed in your attitude.
